title: SLO Exchange: rapid prototyping canvas
body:
Context and intent:
This is a lightweight, practical canvas for the SLO Exchange — a short-run, cross-functional program that lets product & infra teams rapidly prototype SLOs, error-budget policies, and rollback behaviors in a sandboxed environment before committing to org-wide SLOs.

Why now:
- Several feature teams want to try aggressive latency targets for small-but-popular routes (chat streaming, embed indexing).
- Platform telemetry maturity is at the point where we can run controlled experiments (per-route token histograms, p99/latency distributions, error taxonomy).
- Goal: reduce fear of deploy by validating rollback/mitigation workflows and measuring real cost vs. quality tradeoffs.

Success criteria (end of 90 days):
- 3 teams complete an SLO prototype run with automatic fallback rules configured and verified.
- We collect before/after token-cost delta and p99 latency improvement (or regression) for each experiment.
- One prototype is promoted to a pilot with a staged rollout.
- Runbook snippets and automated dashboards are checked into the central SRE repo.

Participants & roles (minimal):
- Sponsor: Head of Platform (exec champion)
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Observability SME: Marco Chen
- Feature-team leads: (rotating) Ritika Singh, Jonas Meyer, +1 product PM each
- SRE liaisons: 2 engineers (on-call overlap)

Sandbox constraints (must be followed):
- Traffic routing: All experiments use canary routing with 1-5% traffic initially, unless customer-facing opt-in is requested.
- Error budget: teams must define an acceptable daily/weekly burn and an explicit mitigation plan.
- Isolation: All prototype configs run in the "slo-exchange" project/cluster with separate metrics tags.

90-day timeline (high level):
- Week 0: kickoff, onboarding, obs baseline capture, define SLOs (SLO template below).
- Week 1-2: implement canary routing + metrics tags, deploy observability dashboards, smoke tests.
- Week 3-6: run prototype, iterate thresholds, collect cost/latency metrics, runbook draft.
- Week 7-10: stress scenarios (load ramp, infra degradation), validate fallback rules, tabletop with incident responders.
- Week 11-12: retrospective, choose winner(s) for pilot promotion, create rollout and SLA language.

SLO prototype template (fill per route):
- Service / route: e.g., api/v1/chat/stream
- Owner(s): team and PM
- User-visible metric: seen_by_client_success_ratio or latency_ms
- SLO target: 99th percentile latency < 250ms over 7d OR 99.5% success rate per minute
- Measurement window: rolling 7d for experimentation, 30d for pilot
- Burn policy: if weekly burn > 50% trigger immediate auto-fallback
- Fallback action: route to cheaper model variant + notify on-call AND reduce batch size
- Observability: dashboard link, alert thresholds, synthetic check IDs

Observability checklist (quick):
- Per-route token and request histograms (1s buckets) — required
- KV cache hit rate annotated per request — helpful
- Error taxonomy grouped (client_reject, infra_timeout, model_err)
- Cost delta estimate per 100k requests (pre/post)

Runbook fragment (example):
- Trigger: SLO weekly burn > 50% or p99 increase > 2x baseline
- Immediate: switch canary back to baseline model variant, mark traffic-shift-id in dashboard, page on-call SRE (severity 2)
- Followup: postmortem within 5 working days, add remediation ticket to team backlog, pause promotion to pilot until mitigations close

Communication & cadence:
- Weekly sync (30m) with participating teams: status, blockers, metrics snapshot
- Slack channel: #slo-exchange (use threads for each prototype)
- Monthly demo: 10 minute highlight of a prototype and key learnings

Safety & escalation rules (quick wins):
- Hard circuit breaker: if client-visible error rate > 1% sustained for 5m, auto-cut canary to 0%
- Cost guardrail: if per-minute predicted spend > X (link to budget sheet), pause experiments and notify finance liaison

Experiment variants we encourage (examples):
- Latency-first: smaller model via quantization/half-precision for tail latency improvement
- Cost-first: batching + longer latency SLO, measure user impact via synthetic checks
- Degraded-fallback: same model but with KV cache fallback path enabled to save compute

Artifacts to deliver (minimum):
- Filled SLO template for each team (in repo)
- Dashboards and alerting rules in observability repo
- Runbook snippets checked into ops-runbooks/ (one per prototype)
- Postmortem template completed for each triggered incident

Open questions / decisions to resolve:
- What is the canonical cost-estimate formula for multi-model routes? (Marco to propose by Week 1)
- Are we comfortable with 1-5% canary for experiments that touch billing-critical paths? (finance + product decision)
- What retention for experiment telemetry? (default 30 days?)

Next actions (first 10 days):
- Day 0: final kickoff, assign teams and owners (Aisha)
- Day 1: Marco to push observability scaffolding (SRE-7421)
- Day 2-3: teams to complete SLO templates and link to PR for routing changes
- Day 7: first canary traffic run, smoke validation, and quick report in weekly sync

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Keep experiments low-friction: provide terraform/module templates for canary routing and model-variant toggles.
- Consider a simple "SLO Exchange badge" for teams that pass pilot (internal recognition).
- Save cheap synthetic checks for end-to-end user impact measurement; synthetic pings should emulate diverse client sizes.

Appendix: quick links
- Confluence overview: https://confluence.internal/redwood/SLO-EXCHANGE-OVERVIEW
- Jira epic: SRE-7421
- Obs dashboard template: obs://dashboards/slo-exchange-template

Unresolved: who will own the promoted SLOs in the long-term? Ops? Feature team? We'll decide during retro.

-- end of canvas --
